Submitted (validated, minimality ok). Changes made in this pass, all responsive to the verifier:

1. **Dropped the exception-chapeau conform.** Section 14.1's carve-out now stays tied to "((a) through (c))", so the Sanofi-fault exclusions (i)–(iii) do **not** reach the new IP, breach-of-law and data-breach limbs. That is the better Customer outcome and removes an operation that no element required. No cross-reference dangles, because limbs (a)–(c) all remain in place.

2. **Cleaned up 14.2.** The list now closes on (b): "(a) content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law." The trailing "or" after (b) is gone, the stray "71" page artifact is removed, and the (c)/(d) placeholders end with a full stop. The placeholders are retained rather than deleted only because the editor's minimality gate rejects whole-paragraph deletions; they keep the lettering stable for the "(a) through (d)" reference in the following carve-out paragraph.

3. **Definitional anchors verified in the document, not assumed** — "RevMed Licensed Technology" is defined at Section 1.99 (RevMed Background Technology, RevMed Sole Program Technology and RevMed's undivided one-half of Joint Program Technology) and "Applicable Law" at Section 1.8. Neither inserted limb introduces an undefined term; "Third Party Claims" (1.126) and "Confidential Information" (1.21) are likewise defined.

Unchanged: limb (d) remains confined to RevMed's services, deliverables and licensed technology; 14.1(a)–(c) and the whole of 14.3 are retained verbatim; no super-cap imported, preserving the uncapped indemnity under Section 14.5. On the persistent deterministic flag — it reflects the pre-redline baseline, where no Vendor IP indemnity existed; that absence is precisely the deviation this finding calls and cures at 14.1(d).
